papers.title: Optimization of Advertising Bidding Model With Generative AI and Deep Reinforcement Learning Collaboration: Design and Validation of Closed‐Loop Simulation Framework
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Real‐time bidding (RTB) requires decisions in milliseconds under nonstationary market dynamics; traditional optimization and online RL suffer from sample efficiency, stability and generalization limitations. This study proposes a closed‐loop simulation framework coupling generative AI with deep reinforcement learning. papers.summary: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies fail on memory tasks, behaviour that depends on events observed long before the current frame, because their training data is overwhelmingly Markov and mapping episodic memory directly to action chunks is hard. Yet the same policy, finetuned once to follow a privileged oracle's grounded-subgoal text, nearly solves these tasks: the difficulty lies entirely in mapping memory to a grounded symbolic subgoal. papers.title: Preserve or Repair? Selective Boundary Policy for a World Action Model
papers.summary: Action-chunked robot policies replan at chunk boundaries, where discontinuities may arise from execution artifacts or encode necessary task transitions such as grasping, pulling, and releasing. This ambiguity makes uniform boundary handling suboptimal: preserving every boundary leaves harmful jumps uncorrected, whereas smoothing every boundary can weaken intentional transitions. We formulate action-chunk boundary handling as a selective preserve-or-repair policy and introduce Selective Boundary Policy (SBP), a lightweight executor-side module for frozen Fast-WAM execution. papers.summary: Managing e-book collections in digital libraries requires high efficiency and accuracy to meet library needs. 中文書名:微流體環境中的智能機器人定位極限 MICROFLUIDIC ENVIRONMENT IN INTELLIGENT ROBOT LOCALIZATION AT THE LIMIT This 777-page English research monograph asks whether intelligent robot localization in microfluidic environments can improve sample-identity probability without increasing contact impulse or carryover. The book contains 30 mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 single-page studies, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. It covers microfluidic flow, optical and multimodal localization, state estimation, data association, closed-loop control, sample identity, uncertainty, blinded fault tests and independent reconstruction. The work is nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim completed clinical testing, proven in-body efficacy or autonomous medical authority. Identity, contact, carryover, purity, calibration and external reconstruction must pass together. papers.summary: Robust 3D reconstruction across varying environmental conditions remains a critical challenge for robotic perception, particularly when transitioning between air and water. papers.summary: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. This work addresses these challenges by integrating soft robotics with computer vision. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. papers.summary: The motion control of robots within swarms depends on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), which could be unavailable in critical environments such as underground facilities, dense urban areas, or zones of conflict. papers.summary: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. Emergency undocking in robotic surgery: an international Delphi consensus study
papers.summary: Emergency undocking in robotic surgery is an uncommon but high-stakes event. Published protocols are predominantly single-institution and specialty-specific, and no multidisciplinary cross-specialty consensus exists. This study aimed to establish expert consensus on the definitions and procedural steps of safe emergency undocking. A four-round modified Delphi study was conducted with an international panel of robotic theatre team members.
